# PDF Designer Overview

## Overview

The PDF Layout Studio lets you design custom PDF tickets that are generated automatically when orders or artwork arrive. You can create templates for **Production Jobs**, **Order Summaries**, **Shipping Labels**, **Packing Slips**, and **QC Checklists**.

Access the studio from **Settings → PDF Layout Studio**, or click the design icon on any existing template to edit it.

---

## The Visual Editor

The editor has three panels:

1. **Left panel – Page setup & elements**
   Set your page size (A4, A5, 4×6, Letter, or custom dimensions in mm). Add elements to the canvas: **Text**, **Rectangle**, **Line**, **QR Code**, **Thumbnail Grid**, or **Jobs Table**.

2. **Centre panel – Canvas preview**
   Drag and resize elements visually. The canvas shows a scaled representation of your page at the dimensions you chose.

3. **Right panel – Properties**
   Select any element on the canvas to edit its exact position (X, Y in mm), size (width, height), font, colour, alignment, and content.

> **Coordinate system**: PDF coordinates use the **bottom-left** corner as the origin (0, 0). X increases to the right, Y increases upward. All values are in millimetres.

---

## Element Types

| Element | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| **Text** | Static labels or dynamic variables (see below) |
| **Rectangle** | Borders, section dividers, background areas |
| **Line** | Horizontal or vertical rules |
| **QR Code** | Scannable codes containing order/job data |
| **Thumbnail Grid** | Grid of job artwork thumbnails for visual reference |
| **Jobs Table** | Itemised list of jobs in the order with automatic pagination |

---

## Dynamic Variables

Use these placeholders inside **Text** or **QR Code** elements. They are replaced with real data at generation time:

- `{order_number}` – the order number
- `{order_code}` – the unique order code
- `{customer_name}` – customer's full name
- `{job_id}` – individual job ID
- `{job_number}` – job sequence number
- `{qty}` – quantity for the job
- `{job_count}` – total number of jobs in the order
- `{date}` – current date
- `{due_date}` – order due date

For QR codes, you can combine variables, e.g. `{order_code}-{job_id}`.

---

## Template Settings

Each template has configuration options:

- **Trigger** – choose when the PDF is generated: *Order Received*, *Artwork Received*, or manual only.
- **Auto-print** – route the generated PDF directly to a PrintNode printer. Select the target printer and number of copies.
- **S3 archiving** – optionally save a copy of every generated ticket to your configured S3 storage bucket.

---

## AI Layout Editor

Click the **AI chat** button in the studio to describe layout changes in plain English. For example:

- *"Move the QR code to the top-right corner"*
- *"Make the customer name bold and 14pt"*
- *"Add a horizontal line below the header"*

The AI will update element positions, sizes, and properties on the canvas.

---

## Previewing & Testing

Use the **Preview** button to render a sample PDF with placeholder data. This lets you check sizing, element placement, and variable substitution before going live.

To test against a real order, use the **Test with Order** option – select an existing order and the system will generate a one-off PDF without affecting the original artwork or triggering any print jobs.

---

## Tips

- **QR codes** are rendered as vector SVG paths, so they stay crisp at any print resolution.
- **Jobs Table** elements automatically paginate if the order contains more jobs than fit on a single page.
- Templates are **per-organisation** – each organisation can maintain its own set of layouts.
- Use **duplicate** to clone an existing template as a starting point for a new design.
